recipe_name: Chicken Scallopini with Lemon Caper Sauce
visual_description: Golden-brown chicken medallions, lightly floured and pan-seared, are the focal point. They are arranged slightly overlapping on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A glossy, pale yellow lemon-caper sauce is spooned generously over the chicken. Bright green capers are scattered throughout the sauce, adding visual texture. Fresh, finely chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a pop of vibrant green. The chicken has a tender, moist interior visible at the edges. The plate features moderate negative space, showcasing the dish clearly. It rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the dish's appealing textures.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Place each breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness to create medallions.
Season flour with salt and pepper. Dredge chicken medallions lightly in seasoned flour. Shake off excess.
Heat olive oil and 15 g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken medallions to pan. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary.
Sear chicken 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30 g butter to pan. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Pour in chicken broth and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Stir in capers and chopped parsley. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return chicken medallions to the pan. Spoon sauce over chicken. Serve immediately.

visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Chili-Tomato Braised Chicken is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone, showcasing a clean, minimalistic composition. A whole, bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, its skin deeply seared to a rich golden-brown, rests centrally. Alongside the chicken, large, tender potato wedges and thick chunks of roasted carrots and celery are arranged naturally, their warm, earthy tones contrasting with the vibrant reddish-brown braising liquid. Wilted, dark green seasonal greens are nestled among the vegetables, adding a subtle color pop. The braising liquid, rich and glossy from the fermented chili and tomato, pools gently around the ingredients, highlighting its depth. A scattering of freshly chopped bright green parsley provides a delicate, fresh garnish. The plating emphasizes natural textures and colors, with ample white space around the dish. The setting features a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, with a clean, minimalist background that includes subtle hints of natural elements like a potted plant.

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (approx. 400g), peeled, cut into large wedges

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deep golden brown and crispy. This takes 8-10 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add chopped onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in smashed garlic, fermented tomato paste, and fermented chili paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return chicken to the pot, skin-side up. Add homemade chicken stock, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 44 minutes.
Add potato wedges to the pot. Continue to braise, covered, for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Stir in seasonal greens until wilted, about 3-5 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve braised chicken and vegetables directly from the pot or plate individually. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: To create a zero-waste chicken stock, simmer chicken bones, trimmings, and vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot tops, celery ends) with water for several hours.
Consider making your own fermented tomato paste or chili paste by lacto-fermenting tomatoes or chilies with salt. This deepens flavor and extends shelf life.
Any leftover braising liquid can be frozen and used as a flavorful base for future soups or stews.

recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Red Wine and Parmesan
visual_description: A single portion of tender braised chicken is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two boneless chicken thighs, golden-brown from initial searing and now richly coated in a deep, glossy red wine and tomato sauce, are nestled together. The sauce, thick and aromatic, pools around the chicken, showcasing small, tender pieces of diced onion and the subtle flecks of herbs. A generous dusting of finely grated white Parmesan cheese melts slightly over the chicken and sauce, creating delicate highlights. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is lightly scattered over the dish, providing a vibrant contrast. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and rich colors in a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with creamy polenta or pasta (e.g., pappardelle, tagliatelle).
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with 3g salt and 1g black pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Do not cook through. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary sprig, thyme sprigs, remaining 2g salt, and 1g black pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Remove rosemary and thyme sprigs. Stir in 30g of grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve immediately.

visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken has a crisp, caramelized exterior, contrasting with its tender, juicy interior. A vibrant lemon-oregano pan sauce, glossy and light yellow, is generously spooned over and around the chicken, forming a natural pool on the plate. Fresh, bright green oregano leaves are visible within the sauce and as a delicate sprig garnish placed beside the chicken. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests near the chicken, ready to be squeezed for extra zest. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a soft, unobtrusive restaurant-style background.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken breasts to the hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a warm plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Add fresh chopped oregano leaves and the juice of half a lemon. Simmer for 3-5 minutes, reducing the sauce slightly.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in cold butter, one piece at a time, until the sauce is emulsified and glossy. Season with salt and pepper as needed.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet, spooning sauce over them. Serve immediately.

recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Mushroom Cream Sauce
visual_description: A single, perfectly seared golden-brown chicken breast rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked whole, displays a crisp, even crust. A rich, creamy mushroom sauce generously coats the chicken and pools elegantly around its base. Sautéed sliced cremini mushrooms are visible within the sauce, alongside vibrant flecks of fresh chopped green parsley. The dish exhibits warm, inviting colors: golden-brown chicken, earthy brown mushrooms, and a pale ivory sauce. Textures are evident: the tender chicken, soft mushrooms, and smooth, velvety sauce. The plating leaves moderate negative space, enhancing the dish's refined, approachable presentation. A simple wooden table surface with standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin complete the modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Accompany with steamed green beans or roasted potatoes.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside on a plate, tent with foil to keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Add diced shallots. Cook for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add chicken stock and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Return chicken to the pan. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer for 1-2 minutes to reheat.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooked to 75°C (167°F).
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing chicken or sautéing mushrooms.
